findings.issue: Move-table sorting reconstructs row data by scraping rendered cell text (Number(textContent) with hardcoded cell offsets), so a markup or formatting change silently corrupts sorting.
findings.suggestion: Keep the MoveRow[] data array in a closure (or module state) and add unit tests for compareValues-driven sorting including the missing-values-last rule.

findings.issue: speciesFromPokemonRefs falls back to the Pokémon API name (e.g. deoxys-normal) when the species map misses an id, producing cards that link to non-species URLs — the exact failure mode the live-data overlay targets.
findings.suggestion: Drop unknown ids instead of falling back, and add a unit test with mixed refs (alternate forms, duplicates, an id absent from the species list).

findings.issue: Pagination math (48/page slicing, page clamping, 'Page n of m', Previous/Next omission) and URL query round-tripping (omit defaults, reset to page 1) are entirely untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract filter/pagination pure functions (stateFromParams/queryFor/matches) and unit-test them: empty q, bogus type values, page beyond total, page=0.

findings.issue: Game select deletes the game query param only when the choice equals the last option; correctness depends on the untested 'sorted by version-group order' invariant in movesSectionHtml.
findings.suggestion: Compute the default game once and compare against it explicitly; test that selecting the default yields a URL without game=.

findings.issue: The renderToken race guard (stale async renders after fast navigation) has no coverage; a regression shows the wrong page's content with no error.
findings.suggestion: Add a Playwright smoke test in app/ that navigates quickly between routes and asserts the final h1; or at minimum factor the router into a testable function.

findings.issue: Static file serving (normalize + prefix check, SPA fallback, config.js injection) is security-relevant and untested.
findings.suggestion: A tiny node test hitting the server with /../, encoded %2e%2e, and deep SPA paths would lock this in cheaply.

findings.issue: latestEnFlavor (last English entry, whitespace collapse) and enName/humanize are the most-reused transforms in the app and have zero tests, though they are trivially unit-testable pure functions.
findings.suggestion: Add a vitest file with the spec's examples (\f collapse, Mr. Mime, Thunder Punch, missing entries).

findings.issue: Hidden-ability detection (first entry wins after id sort, alternate forms dropped) is subtle and untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit test the mapping with a fixture containing hidden and normal entries for the same species id.

findings.issue: esc() is hand-interpolated into every template; one dropped call is an XSS regression nothing in app/ would catch.
findings.suggestion: Consider a tagged-template helper so escaping is structural, or add a test that renders names containing <>&'" and asserts the output.

summary: The agent wrote no tests at all — the repo's own suite is empty and the app leans entirely on the harness's acceptance tests, which will not survive a data-layer or markup refactor. The untested surface is exactly where the risk is: URL filter/pagination state, DOM-scraped move sorting, species/alternate-form mapping, and the static server. Most of the risky logic is pure-function shaped and could be cheaply covered with vitest; its absence makes every future change to these files a leap of faith.
